content:
Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the data patterns:

## Example 1 (2025-08-06)
- History starts around 70.55 and moves up to 71.59 by day 18
- Model forecasts are relatively flat and low-mid range (70.9-71.6)
- True outcomes are significantly higher - ending around 77.51 vs 71.17 predicted

## Example 2 (2025-08-05)
- Very similar to Example 1
- Model forecasts: 70.71-72.95 range
- True outcomes: 70.96-76.75 range

## Example 3 (2025-08-04)
- Almost identical to Example 2
- Model forecasts underperforming the true outcomes

## Example 4 (2025-08-01)
- Slightly different history (starts at 70.42 instead of 70.55)
- Model forecasts again significantly below true outcomes

## Example 5 (2025-07-18)
- History starts at 73.54 (higher than others)
- Model forecasts are also too low
- True outcomes begin at 69.89 and drift lower than predicted

## Key Observations:

Looking at Example 1 more closely:
- The history shows price movement from ~70.5 to ~71.6 over 18 days
- But the TRUE outcome shows prices continuing to rise to 77.51 by day 30
- The model forecasts only go to 71.17 - massively underpredicted

Looking at Example 5:
- History starts higher at 73.54
- But prices then dropped to 69.89 by day 5
- Model forecasts at 69.96, 70.05, 69.47, 69.64 - slightly above true so far


- Model forecasts remain below reality, particularly in the 71-72 range versus 71.72-72.75 actuals

I notice a consistent pattern of model forecasts underperforming true outcomes across all examples. The predictions consistently lag behind actual prices, with significant deviations in the 71-77 range. Sentiment history seems to correlate but not fully explain these discrepancies.

The data reveals systematic underprediction, suggesting the model may be missing key price movement drivers. Particularly striking is the persistent divergence between forecasted and actual prices, especially in the latter half of the observation period.
